mathematics.reason: Maths interpreter: FAIL. The kinematic factor in the decay-length formula is written as √(1 − (E_a/m_a)²), but for a moving axion the physical condition is E_a > m_a, which makes this argument negative and the square root imaginary. The correct relativistic velocity factor is β = √(1 − m_a²/E_a²) = √(1 − (m_a/E_a)²), i.e. the ratio inside the square root should be inverted. Wolfram could not evaluate the check due to a licence issue, so this conclusion rests on direct mathematical reasoning: the decay length λ = γβcτ with γ = E_a/m_a and β = p_a/E_a yields a factor √(E_a² − m_a²)/m_a, which matches √(1 − (m_a/E_a)²), not the expression as printed.

general.reason: The paper's abstract and conclusions explicitly list neutron stars as one of the three key environments ('core-collapse supernovae, neutron stars, and binary neutron star mergers'), but the body text only mentions isolated NSs in one sentence: 'A similar upper bound on the axion-nucleon coupling can be derived from the analysis of the cooling process of cold isolated neutron stars with ages around ~10^5 years [17].' No dedicated subsection, figure, or substantive discussion of NS-based constraints is provided, confirming the mismatch between the abstract's promise and the paper's actual coverage.

judge_panel.reason: The paper's abstract and conclusions explicitly list neutron stars as one of the three key environments ('core-collapse supernovae, neutron stars, and binary neutron star mergers'), but the body text only mentions isolated NSs in one sentence: 'A similar upper bound on the axion-nucleon coupling can be derived from the analysis of the cooling process of cold isolated neutron stars with ages around ~10^5 years [17].' No dedicated subsection, figure, or substantive discussion of NS-based constraints is provided, confirming the mismatch between the abstract's promise and the paper's actual coverage.

The paper explicitly promises coverage of three environments — "core-collapse supernovae, neutron stars, and binary neutron star mergers" and later an "overview of recent results ... namely core-collapse Supernovae (SNe), Neutron Stars (NSs) and Binary Neutron Star (BNS) mergers" — but the only isolated-NS discussion is a single sentence: "A similar upper bound on the axion-nucleon coupling can be derived from the analysis of the cooling process of cold isolated neutron stars with ages around ∼ 10^5 years 17."

The reviewer correctly notes that despite being listed as one of the three main environments in the abstract and introduction, isolated neutron stars are only discussed in a single sentence on page 3: 'A similar upper bound on the axion-nucleon coupling can be derived from the analysis of the cooling process of cold isolated neutron stars with ages around ~ 10^5 years 17.'
